The theoretical guarantees contain substantive errors. Appendix C.3 uses ergodicity to equate conditional and unconditional expectations of finite-horizon invariant-property estimates; ergodicity alone does not justify this step. Methodological novelty is limited relative to classical analog forecasting and delay-coordinate nearest-neighbor prediction; the manuscript also acknowledges that context parroting was previously observed in reference 42. Section F.4 treats finite-trajectory estimates as though they were asymptotic invariant quantities: ergodicity does not make a finite-horizon statistic's conditional expectation independent of the query. These arguments do not establish the stated preservation guarantees for periodic replay.

The algorithmic novelty is limited: the method is nearest-neighbor forecasting in delay coordinates, and Chronos copying was already reported in the cited prior work. Although simplex projection and AutoARIMA are included, their tuning is insufficiently documented, while S-map and Farmer–Sidorowich comparisons are deferred. Moreover, Equation (7) applies an additional 1/k factor to already normalized weights without renormalizing the selected neighbors, so it does not recover its claimed averaging limit. Whether this affects the experimental implementation is unclear.

The interpretation of forecast failures conflates point prediction with trajectory generation. Convergence toward a conditional mean or median can be appropriate under uncertainty, rather than evidence that a model failed to learn dynamics. The manuscript specifies median predictions but does not clearly document a separate sampled-trajectory protocol for invariant metrics. Probabilistic evaluation and individual sampled rollouts are needed to support these conclusions. Positive finite-data Lyapunov estimates from periodic replay also do not establish recovery of chaotic dynamics.

The mechanistic claims exceed the evidence. A representative Chronos example and an analogy with induction heads do not demonstrate that foundation models generally implement context parroting. There are no quantitative copying measurements across models or causal attention-head interventions. Claims about explaining language-model forecasting or determining whether models learned physics should be presented as hypotheses.

Reproducibility is inadequate for the strength of the claims. The supplied reproducibility statement ends without a code link; preprocessing, sample counts, and context settings for the additional scientific datasets are insufficiently specified, as are several inference and estimator settings. The claimed six-orders-of-magnitude computational advantage is unsupported by a timing table or a documented hardware, batching, and measurement protocol.
